cells.uncertainty: Pilot cell: one third-party path (jansson 2.15.1, 282,984 Debian popcon sourcemax installations, captured 2026-11-17) was built, control-verified against the exact nested structure of the control, and given native AFL++ feedback with a stable valid-control differential. Search was the Conan Center recipe-name substring 'json' (24 hits, 3 of them C JSON parsers) plus three targeted C names (jansson, jsmn, parson); adoption was compared with Debian popcon sourcemax counts. json-c (269,736) is within 5% of jansson and was not built; cJSON (150,958) and yyjson (14,868) were not built. No search or standard/runtime inventory has been performed. This pilot cell is incomplete; zero is not evidence of absence.

cells.selection: taglib (4,118) is the only C++ library among the 25 Homebrew hits with a documented local byte/stream API that parses MPEG frame headers. Its MPEG::File over a ByteVectorStream reports version, layer, sample rate, channels, bitrate and duration for both untagged Layer III controls. Higher-ranked mpg123 (12,256) and lame (6,992) are C libraries and belong to the C cell; the C++ hits mp3val, mp3check, mp3blaster, ncmdump and mp3fs are programs without a documented library API.
cells.family: TagLib MPEG frame-header and tag parser; the same TagLib 2.3.2 library as the active mp3_id3v2/cpp taglib entry. This is a separate plain-frame scope, not an independent parser family.
cells.uncertainty: One verified path; no padding. Search is a substring match over all Homebrew formula names and descriptions for six queries, captured 2026-11-17; header-only C++ decoders and vcpkg/Conan packages were not searched. Homebrew installs measure demand for the whole TagLib distribution, mostly as a tag library, not use of its MPEG property API. TagLib parses frame headers and does not decode audio; for CBR streams without Xing/VBRI its duration comes from stream size and the first frame's bitrate. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

Pilot cell: only the highest-adoption Java XML parser engine lead (xerces:xercesImpl 2.12.2, 2,474 deps.dev direct dependents summed over all releases) was built and control-verified. jackson-dataformat-xml, jsoup and xstream score higher but are a data-binding layer, an HTML parser and a serializer, and are logged as non-parser leads. dom4j (both coordinates summed: 3,189) and JDOM are tree builders over a JAXP SAX parser that defaults to the JDK Xerces fork, so they have no tokenizer of its own. The standard javax.xml.parsers path runs OpenJDK's internal repackaged Xerces fork, so both verified Java XML paths share the Apache Xerces2-J family; they are separate, diverged code copies. The xercesImpl release jar has no line tables, so its pinned sources jar is recompiled with -g for line coverage. DOM keeps no attribute order, so attributes are reported sorted per element. Maven Central text search ranks by relevance, not adoption; leads were looked up directly on deps.dev. Two small UTF-8 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, entity, schema, non-UTF-8 or XML 1.1 behaviour.

Pilot cell: one third-party path (saxes 6.0.0, 601,886,067 npm downloads 2026-10-17 to 2026-11-15) was built, verified on two valid namespace controls against the expat oracle, and given parser-derived V8 AFL++ feedback. It is the highest-download lead in the snapshot with its own JavaScript XML 1.0 + Namespaces parser and namespace URI resolution; jsdom (587,846,374) delegates its XML parsing to saxes, and htmlparser2 (526,964,241) is an HTML tokenizer with an xmlMode. sax (490,225,823), fast-xml-parser (426,764,010) and @xmldom/xmldom (326,406,305) have their own parsers and were not run. Downloads were fetched for 19 hand-picked candidates, not every search hit; transitive dependency downloads (jsdom pulls saxes) inflate saxes's count relative to direct use. saxes takes strings, so the adapter decodes bytes with a strict UTF-8 TextDecoder first. Node.js 26.10.0 core has no XML parser API, so the standard count is 0. cells.selection: sabre/xml 4.1.0 (Packagist 39,858,833), a package API over the libxml2 family: Sabre\Xml\Reader extends XMLReader and builds its own Clark-notation element tree. Both valid controls match the expat oracle on elements, attributes, depth, root and text.
cells.uncertainty: Pilot cell, one verified third-party path. The earlier zero count wrongly excluded libxml2-family wrappers; PROTOCOL.md lets a wrapper qualify as a package API with its parser family identified, so sabre/xml is counted with family libxml2 (shared with the standard XMLReader path). symfony/dom-crawler and jms/serializer stay excluded because they only navigate or map an already parsed DOM/SimpleXML tree. The other libxml2-family wrappers (veewee/xml, mtownsend/xml-to-array, saloonphp/xml-wrangler, laravie/parser, orchestra/parser, pear/xml_parser and smaller ones) were not evaluated by the cutoff and remain unresolved, as do the own-code leads prewk/xml-string-streamer and watoki/dom. sabre/xml drops xmlns declarations and text in mixed-content elements by design, so its summary omits namespace declaration counts. Its coverage image uses Ubuntu PHP 8.5.4 with libxml 2.15.2; its AFL++ overlay uses the source-built PHP 8.5.12 and libxml2 2.15.4. The search covers the first 100 hits of five Packagist queries; controls are two small UTF-8 namespace-aware documents without DOCTYPE.
